summary.text: CA9 is the candidate with the strongest and most robust convergent evidence. It leads the overall convergence ranking (score 4.5197) and is the only gene that stays in the overall top ten under random re-weighting (p_top10 0.894). It is up in tumour at RNA (log2FC 6.312) and protein (log2FC 2.269), replicates in TCGA-KIRC (log2FC 9.712), survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (RNA log2FC at purity 1 of 7.787), and single-cell data place 0.976 of its tumour transcripts in RCC cells. Girentuximab reached PHASE_3. DepMap shows no dependency (mean effect 0.051), so CA9 is an antibody, imaging and diagnostic target rather than an essential gene.

A second tier of tumour-up candidates is protein-confirmed, replicated in TCGA-KIRC and purity-robust: SCARB1 (top of the target profile), CD70, NNMT, SLC16A3 (MCT4) and ENPP3. CD70 and ENPP3 already have antibody or ADC programmes. NNMT adds adverse prognosis and supportive ccRCC literature. SCARB1 has no ccRCC literature relations in the corpus, which makes it the most novel of the group. None of these genes is a selective DepMap dependency, so the target calls rest on tumour-restricted expression and tractability, not on essentiality.

The biomarker profile is led by genes lost with proximal-tubule identity: PSAT1, PCK1, ALDH6A1, SLC6A19 and PPP1R1A, together with ALDOB and SLC22A8 in the overall ranking. They are down in tumour at RNA and protein, replicate in TCGA-KIRC and carry significant TCGA survival associations. They are diagnostic and prognostic candidates, not therapeutic targets.

The clinically validated ccRCC axes appear as context, not as data-led discoveries. VHL is the dominant somatic driver, EPAS1 (belzutifan, approved) is the only candidate with ccRCC-selective DepMap dependency, and KDR is an endothelial angiogenesis target. Discovery candidates (COL23A1 and RAB42 in tumour, OLFML2A and JAG2 in stroma, SLC37A2 and LILRB4 in the immune track) are data-ranked hypotheses without dependency evidence.

omics.text: In CPTAC tumour-vs-normal data CA9 is the clearest up-regulated candidate: RNA log2FC 6.312 and protein log2FC 2.269, with a modest positive copy-number cis effect (rho 0.224).

Other tumour-up genes with protein confirmation are SCARB1 (RNA log2FC 2.974, protein 1.837), CD70 (RNA 4.464, protein 2.421), NNMT (RNA 4.67, protein 2.709), SLC16A3 (RNA 3.435, protein 2.279) and ENPP3 (RNA 3.895, protein 1.544).
FABP6 is up at RNA (log2FC 4.006) and protein (log2FC 1.921), and its copy number is gained in 0.573 of tumours with a cis effect of rho 0.309, a plausible dosage contribution.
On the loss side, ALDH6A1 is down at RNA (log2FC -3.399) and protein (log2FC -1.925), with CNV loss frequency 0.355 and a positive cis effect (rho 0.525), consistent with a copy-loss dosage effect.

literature.text: Literature support is concentrated on CA9, CD70 and NNMT. CA9-targeted PET is described as proof-of-concept warranting prospective validation. CD70 is reported as overexpressed in RCC with minimal normal-tissue expression, as a downstream HIF target, and as the subject of 68Ga-labelled single-domain-antibody tracers. NNMT is described as a prognostic biomarker and potential therapeutic target, and selective tool inhibitors exist in a non-ccRCC chemistry paper.

Biomarker literature for the down-regulated genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, ABAT) rests mostly on single bioinformatic or IHC studies. UMOD loss is the most reproduced across independent studies. The corpus has a contradiction for MT1G, which is low in tumour yet linked to poor prognosis when high. FABP1 relations concern colorectal and lung cancer rather than ccRCC, and SCARB1 has no extracted ccRCC literature relations despite strong data support.

external.text: Open Targets drug records separate candidates with clinical programmes from untested ones. CA9 (girentuximab, PHASE_3), CD70 (cusatuzumab, PHASE_2) and ENPP3 (AGS-16C3F, PHASE_2) are membrane proteins accessible to antibodies or ADCs. NNMT, SCARB1 and SLC16A3 have predicted tractability only and no drugs listed.

EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the established ccRCC target with belzutifan approved. DepMap shows a selective but partial dependency (selectivity 0.3, fraction of ccRCC lines dependent 0.208, padj 0.061), and it is not common essential.
VHL is the core driver, mutated in 247 of 511 tumours (frequency 0.483). It has no drug of its own, so the therapeutic route runs through HIF-2alpha downstream.

cells.text: CA9 is tumour-cell intrinsic: RCC cells hold 0.976 of its tumour transcripts (54.7% of RCC cells express it), and tumour cells versus proximal tubule give log2FC 7.739 (padj 0.0189).

Several clinical candidates are microenvironmental rather than tumour-intrinsic. KDR is endothelial (0.951 of transcripts), CD74 is carried mainly by macrophages (0.436), and CXCR4 by CD8 T cells (0.563). EPAS1 transcripts in this scRNA-seq dataset are mostly endothelial (0.365) rather than RCC (0.051). By contrast MET is mainly tumour-cell (0.935). CD70 and NNMT single-cell records carried no evidence ids, so their cell-level split is not quoted; their purity-1 log2FC values support tumour-intrinsic expression, and CD70 has some T/B-cell expression, an off-tumour caveat.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, CA9 expression is assigned to RCC spots (composition-corrected share 0.999), and high-CA9 spots are enriched for RCC neighbours (log2 enrichment 0.381, padj 0.0017). CA9 therefore marks tumour-cell-rich niches.

The microenvironment genes look the same in situ. KDR spots are explained by endothelium (composition-corrected share 0.99, RCC 0.002), and CD74 spots mostly by macrophages (0.637), so their bulk signals come from vessels and immune infiltrate, not tumour cells.

structure.text: Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank candidate sites; they are not evidence that a degrader exists. CA9's best site scores 0.546 (volume 126.8 A3, pocket pLDDT 90.3, one accessible lysine), with ligand-site recall 0.5. The pocket is small and probably the catalytic zinc site, a modest site for a protein already addressed by antibodies.

Among discovery candidates, SLC37A2 has the highest-ranked site (score 0.7403, volume 228.1 A3, 4 accessible lysines, model pLDDT 83.94), with ligand-site recall 1.0 from a single ligand, which is weak support. SLC37A2 is a macrophage protein, so a degrader there would act on immune cells, not tumour cells.
RAB42, a tumour-track candidate, has the next-best site (score 0.5348, mean pLDDT 85.31, 3 accessible lysines), but the pocket is small (37.4 A3) and lacks ligand validation.
The COL23A1 model is poor (mean pLDDT 58.91) with a single 8.0 A3 pocket scoring 0.2342, so it is not a credible degrader site.

discovery.text: The tumour-track discovery lead is COL23A1. It is novel in having no clinical drug, and it is antibody or PROTAC tractable, surface or secreted, with low vital-organ expression (3 nTPM, heart muscle). RCC cells carry 0.881 of its transcripts. It replicates in TCGA (log2FC 5.829) and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour (log2FC at purity 1 of 4.88). It shows no dependency (DepMap mean effect 0.167).

RAB42 is a second tumour-track hypothesis: RCC cells hold 0.627 of its transcripts, there is no clinical drug, vital-organ expression peaks at 2.6 nTPM (lung), and it replicates in TCGA (log2FC 4.371) with a purity-1 log2FC of 3.189. There is no functional or dependency evidence.

The stroma track gives OLFML2A (fibroblast-borne, 0.647 of transcripts; TCGA log2FC 2.372, purity-1 log2FC 1.527; vital-organ expression 27.9 nTPM in colon) and JAG2 (mostly endothelial, 0.487; TCGA log2FC 1.549, purity-1 log2FC 1.061; DepMap mean effect 0.204). Both target the microenvironment, have modest effect sizes and lack functional evidence.

The immune track is mostly infiltration. SLC37A2 is macrophage-borne (0.886) with TCGA log2FC 3.093 that shrinks to 0.619 at purity 1, and LILRB4 (macrophage, 0.933) has TCGA log2FC 3.7 that falls to 0.508 at purity 1. Both bulk signals largely reflect macrophage abundance, so these are immune-cell targets at best. All discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; none is a selective dependency.

validation.text: External replication in TCGA-KIRC is strong for the leading targets: CA9 (log2FC 9.712), CD70 (7.09), ENPP3 (5.557), NNMT (4.685), SCARB1 (3.989) and SLC16A3 (3.291). All stay up when extrapolated to a pure tumour (purity-1 RNA log2FC 7.787, 4.278, 5.278, 5.256, 3.762 and 3.821), so these changes come from tumour cells rather than infiltration.

Prognosis strengthens NNMT: higher expression is adverse in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.301, padj 0.00479). DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency for NNMT (mean effect 0.316), which weakens its case as a functional target.

The independent layers weaken the essentiality case across the board. None of the top candidates is a recurrent somatic driver (VHL is, at frequency 0.483, and PBRM1 at 0.362), and EPAS1 is the only selective DepMap dependency (selectivity 0.3). On the biomarker side ALDH6A1 is weakened by the purity check, since its RNA change shrinks from -3.399 to -1.973 at purity 1, while PSAT1 keeps most of it.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting, the target profile is stable at the top. SCARB1 (p_top10 0.968, rank interval 1 to 8), CA9 (0.941, 1 to 13), SLC16A3 (0.881), CD70 and NNMT (0.88 each), ENPP3 (0.823) and FABP6 (0.803) form the robust target top ten. In the biomarker profile PSAT1 is the most stable call (p_top10 0.986, rank interval 1 to 4), followed by PCK1 (0.889), SLC6A19 (0.881) and PPP1R1A (0.8).

Other positions depend on the chosen weights. In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 is robustly top ten (p_top10 0.894). In the biomarker profile, DUSP9 (p_top10 0.398, with a 90% rank interval reaching 117) and SLPI (p_top10 0.333) are fragile, as are target-profile entries from rank 11 down, such as PNCK (p_top10 0.004).

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most fully on CA9 and CD70: both are tumour-intrinsic, protein-confirmed, TCGA-replicated, literature-backed and clinically addressed. NNMT converges on omics, literature and prognosis but lacks a drug. SCARB1, ENPP3 and SLC16A3 are data-led, with thin or absent ccRCC literature.

The disagreements are informative. The validated clinical axes (VHL, EPAS1) score high in Open Targets but not in the omics convergence, and EPAS1 transcripts are mostly non-tumour in single-cell data. Down-regulated tubule-identity genes (ALDOB, SLC22A8, PSAT1) top the overall and biomarker rankings but are biomarkers, not targets, and literature calling ALDOB a potential target is not supported by its data-only target profile.

targets.rationale: Strongest convergence overall and second in the target profile (p_top10 0.941): tumour-intrinsic (0.976 of transcripts in RCC cells, purity-1 log2FC 7.787), TCGA-replicated (log2FC 9.712), literature-backed and addressed by girentuximab (PHASE_3). No DepMap dependency, so it is an antibody, imaging and diagnostic target.

Tumour-up at RNA (log2FC 4.464) and protein (log2FC 2.421), TCGA-replicated (log2FC 7.09), purity-robust (4.278), membrane-located with clinical antibodies (cusatuzumab PHASE_2) and supporting ccRCC literature. Ranked above SCARB1 despite a lower target-profile score because the literature and drug layers add independent support; some T/B-cell expression is an off-tumour caveat.

Top of the target profile (score 4.1314, p_top10 0.968): tumour-up (RNA log2FC 2.974, protein 1.837), TCGA-replicated (log2FC 3.989), purity-robust (3.762) and genetically associated in Open Targets (0.519). No drug, no ccRCC literature and no dependency, so it is the leading novel target hypothesis.

Tumour-intrinsic and protein-confirmed (RNA log2FC 4.67, protein 2.709, purity-1 5.256), TCGA-replicated (4.685), adverse prognosis (Cox log HR 0.301) and literature support as prognostic marker. No clinical drug and no dependency (mean effect 0.316), so the biomarker call is firmer than the target call.

Tumour-up (RNA log2FC 3.895, protein 1.544), TCGA-replicated (5.557), purity-robust (5.278), apical membrane protein with an ADC (AGS-16C3F, PHASE_2). Robust in the target profile (p_top10 0.823) but has thin ccRCC literature in the corpus.

MCT4 lactate transporter, tumour-up (RNA log2FC 3.435, protein 2.279), TCGA-replicated (3.291), purity-robust (3.821) and stable in the target profile (p_top10 0.881). Predicted tractable but undrugged and not a dependency.
The most robust biomarker call (biomarker score 5.3696, p_top10 0.986): down at RNA (log2FC -3.867) and protein (-1.963), TCGA-replicated (-2.974) and prognostic (Cox log HR 0.43, padj 5.66e-7).

Loss of proximal-tubule gluconeogenic identity: down at RNA (log2FC -4.424) and protein (-1.859), TCGA-replicated (-3.079) and prognostic (Cox log HR -0.415, padj 1.91e-7); stable in the biomarker profile (p_top10 0.889).

Second in overall convergence: down in TCGA (log2FC -4.741), down at protein (-2.273), favourable when high (Cox log HR -0.358) and supported by ccRCC prognostic literature. A lost-expression gene, so not a target.

Strongest prognostic association among the biomarkers (Cox log HR -0.554, padj 9.45e-12) with a copy-loss dosage effect (cis rho 0.525). Placed below PSAT1 and PCK1 because its rank interval is wider (rank_p95 33) and its RNA change shrinks to -1.973 at purity 1.

Not a convergence-led candidate, but the only selective ccRCC DepMap dependency (selectivity 0.3) and the approved belzutifan target. Kept as the clinical benchmark; its transcripts are mostly non-tumour in scRNA-seq (RCC 0.051).

limitations.text: No leading candidate is a selective DepMap dependency; target calls rest on tumour-restricted expression, replication and tractability, not on essentiality.
The biomarker ranking is dominated by proximal-tubule genes whose tumour-vs-normal loss partly reflects cell-of-origin differences; prognosis is univariate Cox in TCGA-KIRC only.
Literature support for most genes comes from single bioinformatic or small IHC studies; CA9 and CD70 translational work is early-stage.
Single-cell records for CD70 and NNMT returned without evidence ids, so their cell-type split is not quoted; down-regulated convergence genes were not profiled at single-cell level.
Molecular-glue-degrader scores rank AlphaFold pockets and do not indicate that a degrader exists.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses; literature counts are by gene symbol and immune-track genes are largely infiltration-driven.
